text:
I’ve only played Replaced for about an hour, but I already like it a lot. The environment looks really good everything feels detailed and well put together. It honestly feels like the devs have done a great job with the overall design.
The melee combat is what surprised me the most. I haven’t really seen this kind of combat in similar games before, and it feels very satisfying to play. It just clicks and makes the experience more fun.
I didn’t run into any performance issues either, which is always a big plus. Overall, even after just an hour, I’m enjoying it and definitely want to keep playing.

Mixed feelings about this game

Scorn is practically a walking simulator

Pros: Beautiful scenery

Cons: Weak soundtrack and almost no sound effects, which don’t suit a world like this. Excessive graininess that can’t be turned off. No backgrounds. Lack of lore or explanations. The looping, confusing environments make for mediocre level design.

I bought it for €3 – a fair price for a short, shallow experience

The concept is great, the game is fun. But it NEEDS a map. I'm dumb, and sometimes I stop playing a game for a while and I definitely don't remember where I've been. I'm lost, I don't know where I am or where I'm supposed to go, and the teleporting doors don't help. I have no idea how to progress and at this point I'm too frustrated to try. I've been going in circles for a while and I'm just tired of it.

First off, visually this game is absolutely stunning. Every chapter looks incredible, and the art direction is top-tier.
​

My main advice to anyone looking at this game: do not buy it expecting Elden Ring or Sekiro. It isn't a Soulsborne game, and judging it by those standards misses what makes it special. It has its own rhythm, structure, and combat identity.
​

The only real hurdle for me is the story. It is deeply rooted in Chinese mythology and heavy Buddhist lore/references. Unless you're already familiar with Journey to the West or Eastern philosophy, a lot of the narrative and nuances are probably going to go right over your head (they certainly did for me).
​

Still, if you appreciate action, amazing boss designs, and breathtaking visual design, it's well worth playing. Just enjoy the ride for what it is.

Very dark soul-y. Not super well made, I wanted to like it, but there's too much of the same and too much backtracking and re-doing what I've already done a hundred times. If you like Salt and Sanctuary and Dark Souls and the likes, i guess this is worth a lookfor a change of.. graphics?

Good game with the underlying potential to be great.

+ Interesting concept/storyline. Some excellent side-quests to fill out the lore.
+ Large gameplay area, lots to explore. Very atmospheric.
+ Well balanced crafting system.
+ Runs maxed out on a 3 year old PC without any issues.

- Large number of side-quests are superfluous and often defuse the tension of the gameplay (it being a survival horror game).
- The first few hours is a slog, especially in higher difficulties.
- The ending was too easily given away by the memory fragments that appear intermittently throughout.
- Stealth mechanic in the game is ineffectual

Overall, a good game but in my personal opinion, the pacing stops it from being a truly great game. Once you get past the rather lethargic start, it picks up and becomes enjoyable.

Have you ever just put a video game in the oven and let it sit about twenty minutes past its cook time? That is the perfect analogy to describe this odd title. Super flashy, super janky, half refined, half deformed, definitely on fire but you're still enjoying every second of the heat... unless your gaming tastes are cynical and you can't get past the scorch marks. For as short as this is, it seems like a promising demo of something bigger, but for as fun as the gunplay is you'll be spending half the time shooting and half the time laughing at the design decisions going on here.

This is exactly the game I've always wanted. I held off on buying it because I thought it would suck, but it was hands down the best tactical strategy game I've ever played. It's like XCOM2 but smoother, more interesting and ALIEN themed. If you played the old Leading Edge Aliens game, this is like that times a thousand. It's like they took that basic idea and improved it in every way. Main campaign took me 39 hours to complete, which makes this game a fantastic deal. Highly recommended, five stars out of five!

Drowns in the contemporary AAA curse of extremely solid core gameplay, with absolutely everything else abandoned broken, hostile to use, and/or at most half finished. Almost all of the cumulative dev effort was wasted on an endless stream of cosmetics instead of fixes and actual gameplay content, and the dev team themselves had no singular spine between them to reject that approach and push for what both fans and the devs themselves wanted the game to be. A total and final butchering of a franchise. Stop waiting for companies to fix games that launch broken.

Good game, although a bit overrated in my opinion.
It wasn't a masterpiece like The Last Of Us or a huge blockbuster like GTA 5 that came out that same year, yet it still delivered a charming and unique experience.
Short and sweet point and click adventure with superb art and enjoyable music. Not much to say, but for that price it's definitely worth playing at least once :)
Really charming game. There are a couple slogs in the last 20% of the game that keep it from being one of the best, but most of it is chill with great personality.

A very fun and addictive game, you start as a simple indie dev working in his garage and you have to make the road to become a top AAA company.

Pros

• Really Funny.
• Great management system.
• Easy to play.
• You will learn about game history.

Cons

• No replay value.
• No competition with others companies.
This was a fun half an hour showcase with a cute little candle and wax based combat. Hope this gets funding and produced into a full length game as it has a lot of potential for good gameplay loop.

Is this the greatest game of all time? No. Are the "open world" segments a drag? Yes. However, the story is good, the combat is fun, the lore is great, and the game runs pretty dang well on release. That is a win in my book and it is worth a play-through for sure!

I am playing this  game with my girlfriend. We really liked little nightmares 2. But while playing this game it was literally so boring that  I saw her yawn with her mouth open the biggest i've ever seen. She must have been pretty tired and bored of running through 50 empty rooms to be yawning like that. We played REANIMAL and never got bored. Trash Devs, Trash Design, Trash Game. 0/10. There was more action in the dump I took this morning.

Personally I don't think this is worth the asking price if there were more modes like firefight or something I'd easily recommend this. As it stands this is a 50% off or gamepass type game.

Don't get me wrong it's fun but you get much better value out of MCC than this single game.

Sadly this game copies TOO much from hollow knight. I understand it is some kind of tribute game and all, but the game just feels like a beta version of a different HK game. Fun to play, but if you compare the price of this game to other similar ones, it's definitely not worth the price

The constant hide and seek and stalker enemy in this game is such BS, it just becomes a boring chore, not even remotely scary or fun, dude walks three steps outside your room and comes right back in before you even leave the closet. Stalker guy has instant death grab, the IV guys have a hit scan ranged attack. The section with Richard in the Tower shotgunning widows was the only time I felt any tension and the only part of the game that didn't suck.

I love Silent Hill, I have my original physical copies of 1-4, Heather pucking up a fetus is my steam avatar but I'm not a fan of the "Silent Hill effect" nonsense, if anyplace can be a Silent Hill than Silent Hill isn't a "special place" after all, lets get back to actual Silent Hill and dodging and fighting monsters in third person.

This game is everything that is wrong with Early Access.  I do not mind an unfinished game, rough starts, poorly optimized engines, etc. in Early Access.  It is Early Access.  Buyer's choice for buying early.  What I do expect is communication as to what is going on with the game.  The developers released a terrible road map upon release, they have not updated it, and they are not even following it.  They have been radio silent on steam.   I am tired of people saying to go to their Discord (BTW, the discord link on the Steam page is broken) or official website forums.   I bought the game on Steam, post your crap on Steam.   These guys took the money and ran.  Steam should stop allowing EA.

After putting almost 100 hours into this game the first week it dropped, this game is definitely a huge win in my book. This game is over the top with different weapons, abilities, and you can soar through the air in literally the most craziest ways imaginable.

Good game overall, and it is completely free with the only paid features being for cosmetics(though they are crazy expensive). Give this game a try! It is a good time killer.

I bought this game because I love Shogun Showdown and this seemed like the same type of game except action/real-time instead of turn based with a feature called Forestrike to basically let you practice because fights need to be executed perfectly. Then, it went into my backlog, but added to my favorites because I really enjoyed the few minutes of what I tried and meant to get back to it. Well I finally picked it up to give it a proper go and it is indeed really good, fun, and actually has a good story that doesn't seem too intrusive in the gameplay. There are a lot of moves and features in here giving you multiple ways you can play and try to execute your fights which is very cool. I still have tons to discover but this is definitely a quality game that's worth the price, especially if you like Shogun Showdown and basically want that except not turn-based.

I have hopes for this game eventually, and I'm impressed by what the developer has done by himself. 

But I'm not going to recommend Killer Bean just yet. Its got charm, its got some humor, the gameplay has potential, but you can 1000% tell this is an early iteration of this game. I cant describe the feeling that I get playing in this early state but its some weird place where  I'm both enjoying it and not enjoying it, like watching a film thats funny bad. Only that film is replaced with the early concept for a "Just Cause" game

Will update in a year or two. Hoping for the best

One of the most outstanding and captivating video game experiences I have ever had the pleasure of playing.  Story, environment, sound, puzzles and mechanics are all a pure joy.  It's rare games like this that make video gaming an interactive form of art that takes you on a journey as someone else and you come out the other side feeling you've experienced and learned something yourself

This is gives you  more Castlevania than Castlevania.
First off, the gameplay is on point. You can read a full review elsewhere, but put simply it's fun, it's tight, it's balanced, and there is a whole lot of it without even getting to the collectibles.
Even rarer, the story and story flavor is insane. The creators put more thought into this than most Castlevania titles, and it's FRESH. No more recycling the same Grimm fairy tales and Japanese Yokai. This game takes some dank Spanish myths and runs with them. A satisfying and unexpected ending caps this game off.
All of this is complemented by a great musical score, truly amazing animation, and solidly disturbing voice-acting.
THIS GAME SATISFIES.

Nice aesthetics and music, but boring gameplay. Repetitive levels, boring plot, a lot of bugs and pointless solutions: you can kill the horse on which you then run away, your shots alert nearby enemies, but if the enemy shoots, his other friends will continue to sleep, etc...
You can pick up chickens and carry them around, thats reason enough for me to recommend this game.

•  Feedback from the attacks feels great. 
   •  The movement that is available from the beginning is really satisfying. 
   •  Level design is focused and keeps you engaged.
   •  Ran into a few bugs here and there (fell through the ground on the part of the tutorial that teaches you how to slide, if you hold the opposite direction after walking through a door the character walks back into the room before the screen fades, money from chests respawns if you exit the screen and come back) but nothing that has prevented me from enjoying the game.
   •  Star of the show is definitely the music! 

 It is more than worth the money I spent on it.

Its a great game with the worst match making in history. If you are even a little above average this game will put you on a team with a daredevil thats actually blind, a penny whos actually 12, and an ultron whos actually racist.
A great little game that I played with people in a few short sittings. Well done to the developer - very fun!

The most "Hades clone" of them all, doesn't feel like there is much of an attempt to make it self stand out from all the others in the genre other than multiplayer which has recently been done better then this. Releasing same week as Hades 2 is some genius planning. For the price of the game alone it is not worth it I Would wait for a good sale. Multiplayer is friends only there is no matchmaking. All of those paid cosmetic packs are over priced and should be in game rewards not paid packs.
Thought this game was scary as a 6 years old. So I thought I would attempt it at 22 years old. It is still scary.

Killer nuns and genetically enhanced rednecks, if it wasn’t a Hitman game, this could easily pass as a Metal Gear entry for how bonkers and downright stupid it gets. I kinda love it.

7/10 - Would drown a man on the toilet again.

Right click on Bioshock remastered, go to manage, then browse local files
In the files, go to Build > Final > BioshockHD.exe
Congratulations, you have now avoided the 2K launcher

I loved it so much I gave it away to three random strangers on the internet. It has a touching story and the most satisfying platforming puzzles I've ever encountered in a game.

Not for the faint of heart, the quick of temper, or the hurting of hands. You'll only finish this game with perseverance and you'll only complete it with immense patience. But it'll be worth it, if these are the kinds of challenges you enjoy.

It is punishing.
It is unforgiving.
It is brutal.
It requires Jedi focus...

Not for the easily distracted or faint of heart.
You "will" die often (like every two seconds)
You get to run across walls in death defying circumstances... what else could you ask for except the next DLC!

There is nothing bad about this game.
It is in fact, the perfect video game.

Great action, engaging story, deep lore, masterful writing, expressive voice acting, Re-playable, easy to pick up yet tough to master, great variety in play styles, no bugs, beautiful graphics

I mean, supermassive has really dropped the ball here. 

This game seemed so interesting at the beginning but man the stealth stuff is buns. 

The last two titles have also been mid as hell. 

Casting of frank stone was the most boring thing in the world  

The devil in me was also tragic. 

You guys need to fix up cause i love the idea of these games but man you guys have been so bad the last few years. 

This game gets a 5/10

Excellent trial and death game. Great atmosphere and music and interesting puzzles with ingenious mechanics. I strongly recommend this.

You will die a lot but the restarts are instant and usually the deaths feel fair - there appears to be a bit of randomisation meaning some attempts will be easier than others and there are a few places where it's difficult to tell which platforms can be used but this is not really a problem because of the trial and error nature of the game.

cant wait for the movie!

Just kidding lol, this game is a masterpiece, just as the original!
As a beta tester from the very beginning of Early Access, conceptualising the worst ending I had for this game isn't even coming close to what they actually did.
Schedule I is basically a Breaking Bad simulator and it's super addictive. I’m really enjoying it so far and hope the dev keeps improving it throughout early access.

B-tier metroidvania
I liked the art and the non-verbal story-telling. This is a good metroidvania for beginners and achievement hunters. The combat is fairly easy and forgiving. There is an overabundance of healing items which makes up for the fact that most save spots don't restore your health.

I wanted to give this a higher tier ranking but the game is just too easy and short. It's definitely still worth playing though.

Yes and no. Act 4 and 5 fall flat on their face at some point and the story drifts off into some really weird stuff but at the end I still enjoyed my time with the game and if its for sale for like 10 bucks i can safely recommend the game. Act 1 - 3 are a joy

It didn’t blow my mind but I enjoyed it enough to do as much as I could in one playthrough. I would barely call it a metroidvania, it’s more simple and straightforward action, a 2D soulslike. Less difficult but adjustable with equips and world mechanics rather than a setting. I liked the lore and the somber, otherworldly feel. Combat felt good for the most part. Beautiful opening cutscene that draws you in, but it doesn’t really manage to maintain that initial awe.
